titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Azariah on Clean and Unclean Food, and in Praise of Wisdom (ch. 91)
part: ch. 91 — Azariah on Clean and Unclean Food, and in Praise of Wisdom
about: Azariah's address continues. He recites the food laws of Leviticus 11 and Deuteronomy 14: the clean animals that chew the cud and part the hoof, the unclean beasts, the fish with fins and scales, the unclean birds and swarming creatures, and the rule that touching a carcass makes one unclean until evening. He tells the people to keep these laws, so as to be blessed in the land God gave them for the sake of Zion, and then turns to the queen. He praises her wisdom, which he puts second only to Solomon's: she tore down idols, cleansed her people, and was named Makeda, ‘not so’, for the things she rejected. He closes with a long praise of Wisdom as mother, treasure, healer and light, all from God, and says that Zion has come to Ethiopia by God's will, to guide Menelik, called David.

sentences.t: ፺፩ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ዘይበልዑ ፡ ንጹሕ ፡ ወርኩስ ።
sentences.l: 91. This which-they-eat clean and-unclean.
sentences.i: Chapter 91: On what may be eaten, the clean and the unclean.
sentences.n: Chapter heading, a unit of its own. ዘንተ is the accusative of ዝንቱ ‘this’, used as the title-object (‘this [concerning]’), as in earlier headings. ዘይበልዑ is ዘ- ‘which’ + ይበልዑ, 3mp imperfect of በልዐ ‘eat’. ንጹሕ ‘clean’ and ርኩስ ‘unclean’ (the ወ- of ወርኩስ is ‘and’) are the two terms of the Levitical food law, taken up in Leviticus 11 and Deuteronomy 14.

sentences.t: ወዝንቱ ፡ ዘትበልዑ ፡ ንጹሕ ፡ ወዘኢኮነ ፡ ንጹሕ ፤
sentences.l: And-this which-you-eat clean and-which-not-is clean;
sentences.i: These are the clean things that you may eat, and those that are not clean:
sentences.n: ወዝንቱ is ወ- ‘and’ + ዝንቱ ‘this’. ዘትበልዑ is ዘ- + ትበልዑ, 2mp imperfect ‘you eat’; ዘኢኮነ is ዘ- ‘which’ + ኢ- ‘not’ + ኮነ ‘is/was’. Verb-forms in -ኡ mark the plural ‘you’; the speaker is Azariah, still addressing the people, and what follows is a summary of Leviticus 11:2-8 and Deuteronomy 14:3-8, with the sequence of land animals, fish, birds and swarming creatures.

sentences.t: ላህም ፡ በግዕ ፡ ወጠሊ ፡ ሐርጌ ፡ ሀየል ፡ ወይጠል ፡ ቶራ ፡ ድስክነ ፡ ወውዕላ ፡ ዓርጋ ፡ ወዝራት ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ እንስሳ ፡ ዘንፉቅ ፡ ሰኰናሁ ፡ ወጽፈሪሁ ፡ ብልዑ ፡ ወዘይትመሰኳዕ ፡ ብልዑ ፤
sentences.l: Ox sheep and-kid(?) harge(?) stag and-ibex(?) tora(?) dəskən(?) and-wəʿela(?) ʿarga(?) and-zərat(?) and-every beast which-cloven hoof-his and-claw-his eat and-which-chews-cud eat;
sentences.i: Oxen, sheep, the kid or gazelle, the ḥärge (?), the stag, the ibex (?), the tora (?), the dəskən (?), the wəʿela (?), the ʿarga (?) and the zərat (?), and every beast whose hoof and claw are cloven: eat; and whatever chews the cud: eat.
sentences.n: Read this as a list: the ወ- falls between groups, not on every name. ላህም ‘ox/cattle’ and በግዕ ‘sheep’ are sure; ጠሊ ‘kid, gazelle’ and ሀየል ‘stag’ are good Geʿez words. The next names are the animals of Deuteronomy 14:4-5 (ox, sheep, goat, hart, gazelle, roebuck, wild goat, antelope, wild ox, chamois) and I cannot match them with confidence: ሐርጌ is unknown (an antelope or a kid, ?), ይጠል (ወይጠል, taken here as ወ- ‘and’ + a word for ‘ibex’; an earlier part glosses the ወ as part of the word, ?), ቶራ, ድስክነ (resembling Hebrew dishon, ?), ውዕላ (ibex or wild goat, ?), ዓርጋ and ዝራት (perhaps the giraffe, Hebrew zemer, ?) are all uncertain, and the translations are guesses. ዘንፉቅ ሰኰናሁ ወጽፈሪሁ ‘whose hoof and claw is cloven’ (ዘ- + ንፉቅ ‘cloven, split’ + ‘his’) is the rule of Leviticus 11:3. ብልዑ is the 2mp imperative ‘eat!’. ዘይትመሰኳዕ is ዘ- + 3ms imperfect of ተመሰኰዐ ‘chew the cud’ (tä-stem), the other half of the rule: both signs together make an animal clean.

sentences.t: ወዝንቱሰ ፡ ዘኢትበልዑ ፡ እምውስተ ፡ ዘይትመሰኳዕ ፡ ወዘንፉቅ ፡ ሰኰናሁ ፡ ገመል ፡ ወዳሲጳዳ ፡ ወካርግልዮን ፡ እስመ ፡ ይትመሰኵዑ ፡ ወኢኮነ ፡ ንፉቅ ፡ ጽፈሪሆሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-this-indeed which-not-you-eat from-among which-chews-cud and-which-cloven hoof-his: camel and-dasipada and-karglyon, for they-chew-cud and-not-is cloven claw-their;
sentences.i: But these you shall not eat, of those that chew the cud or have a cloven hoof: the camel, the hare (?), and the coney (?), for they chew the cud but their claws are not cloven.
sentences.n: ወዝንቱሰ is ወ- + ዝንቱ + the contrastive enclitic -ሰ ‘but as for this’. ኢትበልዑ (negative + imperfect) is the plain prohibition. The line follows Leviticus 11:4-6 (camel, coney, hare) and Deuteronomy 14:7. ገመል is the camel. ዳሲጳዳ looks like Greek dasypous ‘rough-foot’, the Septuagint's word for the hare (?); ካርግልዮን probably reflects Greek choirogryllios, the Septuagint's rendering of the Hebrew shafan, the coney or hyrax (?). Both are transliterated from Greek, and the identifications are not certain. ይትመሰኵዑ is the plural of the verb in the last unit; ጽፈሪሆሙ ‘their claws’ (suffix -ሆሙ, 3mp).

sentences.t: ወዝእብ ፡ ወሐራዊያ ፡ ኢትብልዑ ፡ እስመ ፡ ንፉቅ ፡ ሰኰናሆሙ ፡ ወኢይትመሰኵዑ ፡ ርኩሳን ፡ ኢትብልዑ ፤
sentences.l: And-wolf(?) and-harawiya(?) not-eat, for cloven hoof-their and-not-they-chew-cud; unclean not-eat;
sentences.i: You shall not eat the pig (?) or the ḥarawiya (?), because their hoofs are cloven but they do not chew the cud; they are unclean, so do not eat them.
sentences.n: The pig of Leviticus 11:7 and Deuteronomy 14:8 (cloven-footed, no cud) is what the reasoning describes. ዝእብ ordinarily means ‘wolf’ or ‘hyena’, and ሐራዊያ is a word I cannot place; I take the pair to stand for the pig and the wild boar (?). ኢትብልዑ is a prohibition; ርኩሳን is the plural of ርኩስ ‘unclean’, here a predicate (‘being unclean’).

sentences.t: በውስተ ፡ ማይ ፡ ዘቦ ፡ ክንፈ ፡ ወቅሣረ ፡ ብልዑ ፡ ወእምኔሁ ፡ ርኩሰ ፡ ኢትብልዑ ፤
sentences.l: In-water which-has fin and-scale eat, and-from-it unclean not-eat;
sentences.i: Of the creatures in the water, eat what has fins and scales; but eat nothing unclean among them.
sentences.n: ዘቦ is ዘ- ‘which’ + ቦ ‘there is to/with it’, the usual way of saying ‘which has’. ክንፈ ‘fin’ (ክንፍ ‘wing, fin’) and ቅሣረ ‘scale’ stand in the accusative -ኧ after the verb. ወእምኔሁ is ወ- + እም ‘from’ + -ኔሁ ‘it’, partitive: ‘out of them’. ርኩሰ is the accusative of ርኩስ, ‘anything unclean’. Compare Leviticus 11:9-12 and Deuteronomy 14:9-10.

sentences.t: ወእምነ ፡ ውስተ ፡ አዕዋፍ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘንጹሕ ፡ ብልዑ ፡ ወዘኢትበልዑ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ንስር ፡ ጊጳ ፡ ኤልያጣን ፡ ግሪጳ ፡ ሆባይ ፡ ወዘአምሳሊሁ ፡ ቋዕ ፡ ሰገኖ ፡ ግላውቃ ፡ ለሮን ፡ አሮድዮን ፡ ቃቃኖን ፡ ኢብን ፡ ቀጣራቃጤን ፡ ጒዛ ፡ ሂጳጳ ፡ ጒጓ ፡ ወኣባጒንባሕ ፡ ወክራድዮን ፡ ጳርፋርዮና ፡ ጽግነት ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ዘርኵስ ፤
sentences.l: And-from among birds all which-clean eat, and-which-not-you-eat this: eagle, gipa(?), elyatan(?), gripa, hobay(?) and-of-likeness-his; raven, sägäno(?), glawqa, laron, arodyon, qaqanon(?), ibn, qatarqaten, guza(?), hipapa(?), gugwa(?) and-abagwənbah(?), and-kradyon, parparyona, ṣəgnet(?); this which-uncleanness;
sentences.i: Of the birds, eat any that is clean; but these you shall not eat: the eagle, the gipa (?), the elyatan (?), the gripa, the hobay (?) and its kind; the raven, the sägäno (?), the glauqa, the laron, the arodyon, the qaqanon (?), the ibn, the qatarqaten, the guza (?), the hipapa (?), the gugwa (?), the abagwənbah (?), the kradyon, the parparyona and the ṣəgnet (?). These are unclean.
sentences.n: The unclean birds of Leviticus 11:13-19 and Deuteronomy 14:12-18. Many of the names are Greek words of the Septuagint list, written in Geʿez letters, and several are known only from this list, so the identifications are uncertain: ንስር is the eagle; ግሪጳ is Greek gryps ‘griffon vulture’ and ጊጳ perhaps gyps ‘vulture’ (?); ኤልያጣን may come from Greek haliaetos ‘sea eagle’ (?); ቋዕ is the raven; ግላውቃ is Greek glaux ‘owl’; ለሮን is Greek laros ‘gull’; አሮድዮን is Greek erodios ‘heron’; ኢብን is Greek ibis; ቀጣራቃጤን is Greek katarraktes ‘cormorant or gull’ (?); ክራድዮን is Greek charadrios ‘plover’; ጳርፋርዮና is Greek porphyrion ‘purple gallinule’ (?); ሂጳጳ may be epops ‘hoopoe’ (?). Left unidentified: ሆባይ, ሰገኖ, ቃቃኖን (possibly kyknos ‘swan’ or kokkyx ‘cuckoo’, ?), ጒዛ, ጒጓ, ወኣባጒንባሕ (possibly ‘father of …’, ?), ጽግነት. ወዘአምሳሊሁ is ወ- + ዘ- + አምሳል ‘likeness’ + -ሁ, ‘and what is like it’, Leviticus' ‘after its kind’; ዘርኵስ is ዘ- ‘of’ + ርኵስ, ‘of uncleanness’, a predicate: ‘these are of uncleanness’.

sentences.t: ወዘኢትበልዑ ፡ ደገብያ ፡ ወዘአምሳሉ ፡ አቃጣን ፡ ወዘአምሳሉ ፡ አፍዮማክን ፡ ወዘአምሳሉ ፡ አንበጣ ፡ ወዘአምሳሉ ፤
sentences.l: And-which-not-you-eat dägäbya and-of-likeness-its aqaṭan and-of-likeness-its afyomakən and-of-likeness-its locust and-of-likeness-its;
sentences.i: And you shall not eat the dägäbya (?) and its kind, the aqaṭan (?) and its kind, the afyomakən and its kind, the locust and its kind, and its kind.
sentences.n: The winged swarming things of Leviticus 11:21-22, whose Septuagint names are the Greek bruchos, attakes, akris and ophiomachês. አንበጣ ‘locust’ is sure; አፍዮማክን reflects Greek ophiomachês ‘snake-fighter’, one of the locust kinds in the Septuagint (?); አቃጣን may be attakes (?); ደገብያ I cannot place (?). The unit ends with a bare ወዘአምሳሉ ‘and what is like it’ that has no noun after it; as printed, a name has probably dropped out, and I keep it so.

sentences.t: እምነ ፡ ዘይሰርር ፡ በበ፪ ፡ በበ፬ ፡ ወበበ፮ ፡ እግሩ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ርኩስ ፡ ሥጋሆሙ ፡ ኢትብልዑ ፡ ወበድኖሙ ፡ ኢትግስሱ ፡ ወዘገሰሰ ፡ በድኖሙ ፡ እስከ ፡ ሰርክ ፡ ርኩስ ፡ ውእቱ ።
sentences.l: From which-creeps by-twos by-fours and-by-sixes foot-its it unclean; flesh-their not-eat, and-carcass-their not-touch; and-who touched carcass-their until evening unclean he.
sentences.i: Of whatever creeps along on two, four or six feet: it is unclean. Do not eat their flesh, and do not touch their carcasses; whoever touches their carcasses is unclean until evening.
sentences.n: ዘይሰርር is ዘ- + 3ms imperfect of ሰረረ, which I take as ‘creep, move along’ (?). The distributive በበ፪ is በበ- ‘by, each’ + the numeral, ‘by twos’ (and so በበ፬ ‘by fours’, ወበበ፮ ‘by sixes’); እግሩ ‘its feet’ gives the manner. Numerals are shown in Ethiopic digits. The rule on touching a carcass is that of Leviticus 11:24-28 (‘unclean until evening’). ኢትግስሱ is a prohibition, ‘do not touch’ (ገሰሰ); ወዘገሰሰ is ወ- + ዘ- + 3ms perfect, ‘and whoever touched’. በድን ‘carcass’.

sentences.t: ዘንተኬ ፡ ነገርናክሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትዕቀቡ ፡ ወትግበሩ ፡ ፍርሀተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ትትባረኩ ፡ በዛቲ ፡ ምድርክሙ ፡ እንተ ፡ ወሀበክሙ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ በእንተ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ እስመ ፡ ተኀረይክሙ ፡ በእንቲአሃ ፤
sentences.l: This-indeed we-told-you that you-keep and-do fear-of God, that you-be-blessed in-this land-your which gave-you God for-sake-of Zion heavenly ark-of law-his of-God, for you-were-chosen on-account-of-her;
sentences.i: We have told you this so that you may keep it and practise the fear of God, and so be blessed in this land of yours, which God gave you for the sake of heavenly Zion, the ark of God's law, for you were chosen on her account.
sentences.n: Azariah's own comment on the food law. ዘንተኬ is ዘንተ ‘this’ (accusative) + the emphatic -ኬ ‘indeed, now’. ነገርናክሙ is ነገረ ‘tell’, 1cp perfect + -ክሙ ‘you (pl)’. ከመ introduces purpose, and ትዕቀቡ ወትግበሩ are subjunctive 2mp (‘that you keep and do’); ፍርሀተ እግዚኣብሔር is ‘fear of God’, in the construct state (ፍርሀተ ‘fear-of’) and also object of ‘do’. ትትባረኩ is the tä-stem of ባረከ, ‘be blessed’. ጽዮን ሰማያዊት ታቦተ ሕጉ is the Zion theology: Zion is the ark (ታቦት), here ‘heavenly’ because she is the earthly copy of a heavenly thing; the construct ታቦተ ‘ark-of’ governs ሕጉ ‘his law’, and ለእግዚኣብሔር repeats the owner (‘of God’), the doubling Geʿez likes. ተኀረይክሙ is the passive of ኀረየ ‘choose’, 2mp perfect.

sentences.t: ወአበዊነሰ ፡ ተመነኑ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘነሥኦሙ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ትዕቀብክሙ ፡ ለክሙ ፡ ወለዘርእክሙ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: But-fathers-our were-bereft(?) because which-took-them God Zion ark-of law-his of-God; she-will-keep-you to-you and-to-seed-your until for-ever;
sentences.i: But our fathers were bereft (?), because God took Zion from them, the ark of his law; she will keep you and your descendants for ever.
sentences.n: ወአበዊነሰ is ወ- ‘and/but’ + አበው ‘fathers’ (plural of አብ) + -ነ ‘our’ + the contrastive -ሰ: ‘but our fathers’, the Israelites at Jerusalem. ተመነኑ is a 3mp perfect I cannot place with confidence: perhaps ‘they were made poor, bereft’ (?). ዘነሥኦሙ is ዘ- ‘what’ + ነሥአ ‘take’ + -ሙ ‘them’; by በእንተ ዘ- ‘because’; whether ‘took from them’ or ‘took them’ is not clear (?). ትዕቀብክሙ is 3fs imperfect of ዐቀበ ‘keep’ + -ክሙ ‘you’, the subject being feminine ጽዮን; ለክሙ ወለዘርእክሙ ‘for you and your seed’ repeats the object with ለ-, and ለዓለም ‘for ever’ (lit. ‘to the age’). The promise recalls Genesis 17:7.

sentences.t: ወይባርክ ፡ ፍሬ ፡ ምድርክሙ ፡ ወያብዝኅ ፡ እንስሳክሙ ፡ ወይዕቀብ ፡ ደቂቅክሙ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ዘትትመሐፀኑ ፡ ወአንቲኒ ፡ እግዝእትየ ፡ ጥበብኪ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ዘተዐደወ ፡ እምጥበበ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ዘከማኪ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘይትማሰላ ፡ ለኅሊናኪ ፡ አኮ ፡ ምክረ ፡ አንስት ፡ ባሕቱ ፡ ዘተፈጥረ ፡ እስከ ፡ ይእዜ ፡ አላ ፡ እምክረ ፡ ተባዕትኒ ፡ ፈድፈደ ፡ አእምሮ ፡ ልብኪ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘይትማሰለኪ ፡ በብዝኀ ፡ አእምሮትኪ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ እግዚእየ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-bless fruit-of land-your and-multiply cattle-your and-keep children-your in-all in-which you-entrust(?); and-you-indeed my-lady wisdom-your good which-surpasses than-wisdom-of man, who-like-you not-is who-resembles to-mind-your, not counsel-of women but which-was-created until now, but than-counsel-of men-also exceeds knowledge-of heart-your, and-not-is who-resembles-you in-abundance-of knowledge-your except Solomon my-lord;
sentences.i: May he bless the fruit of your land, multiply your cattle, and keep your children in everything in which you put your trust (?). And you also, my lady: your wisdom is good, surpassing the wisdom of men; there is no one like you, and nothing that matches your mind. It is not the counsel of women, nor of anything made until now, but the knowledge of your heart goes beyond even the counsel of men; and none equals you in the abundance of your knowledge except Solomon, my lord;
sentences.n: The first three verbs (ወይባርክ, ወያብዝኅ, ወይዕቀብ) are 3ms jussive, ‘let him bless, multiply, keep’, with God as subject, so a blessing rather than a statement. ዘትትመሐፀኑ is ዘ- + tä-stem 2mp imperfect of መሐፀነ, which I read as ‘entrust yourselves, take refuge’ (?). Azariah then turns to the queen: ወአንቲኒ ‘and you also’ (-ኒ emphatic), እግዝእትየ ‘my lady’. ዘተዐደወ እምጥበበ ሰብእ is ዘ- + 3ms perfect ‘surpassed’ + እም ‘than’; ጥበበ is the construct of ጥበብ ‘wisdom-of’. ዘከማኪ is ዘ- + ከማ ‘like’ + -ኪ ‘you (fs)’, and አልቦ ‘there is not’ opens both ‘none like you’ and ‘nothing that resembles’; ዘይትማሰላ ለኅሊናኪ is the tä-ma stem of መሰለ ‘be like’, with ለ- marking what is matched (‘your mind’). ባሕቱ ‘but’ here is awkward, and I read አኮ … ባሕቱ ዘተፈጥረ እስከ ይእዜ as ‘not women's counsel, nor of anything created to this day’ (?). ፈድፈደ ‘exceeds’. በብዝኀ is በ- + the construct ብዝኀ ‘abundance-of’. Solomon is the single exception, as in ch. 90 (‘my lord’, the king). This unit has about forty words, under the usual limit and with no ፤ inside to cut at.

sentences.t: ወእምሰሎሞንኒ ፡ ተዐደወ ፡ ጥበብኪ ፡ እስከ ፡ ትስሕቢ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ኀይለ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ በአሕባለ ፡ አእምሮትኪ ፡ ወነሠትኪ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ጣዖቶሙ ፡ ወደምሰስኪ ፡ አ ፡ ምሳሊሆሙ ፡ ወአንጻሕኪ ፡ ርኵሰ ፡ እምሕዝብኪ ፡ እስመ ፡ አሰሰልኪ ፡ ዘጸልአ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እምላዕሌሆሙ ፡ ወለስምኪኒ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አስተዳለዎ ፡ ዘሰመየኪ ፡ ማክዳ ፡ ወትርጒምናሁ ፡ አኮ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ብሂል ፤
sentences.l: And-than-Solomon-also surpasses wisdom-your until you-draw sons-of host-of Israel and-ark-of law-his of-God by-cords-of knowledge-your, and-you-tore-down house-of idols-their and-destroyed likenesses-their and-cleansed uncleanness from-people-your, for you-removed what hated God from-upon-them; and-for-name-your-also God prepared-it who-named-you Makeda, and-interpretation-its not thus saying;
sentences.i: Your wisdom surpasses even Solomon's, so that you drew in the sons of the host of Israel and the ark of God's law with the cords of your understanding (?). You tore down the house of their idols, destroyed their images, and cleansed uncleanness from your people, for you removed from them what God hated. For your name also God prepared it, who named you Makeda; and its interpretation is: ‘not so’.
sentences.n: ወእምሰሎሞንኒ is ወ- + እም ‘than’ + ሰሎሞን + -ኒ ‘also, even’. ተዐደወ ‘surpassed’ takes ጥበብኪ ‘your wisdom’ as subject. ትስሕቢ is 2fs imperfect of ሰሐበ ‘draw, drag’; ደቂቀ ኀይለ እስራኤል is a double construct, ‘sons of host of Israel’ (‘the Israelite host’). በአሕባለ አእምሮትኪ is በ- ‘by’ + አሕባል ‘cords’ (plural of ሐብል) in the construct + ‘knowledge’ + -ኪ: ‘by the cords of your knowledge’, an image of leading by cords, as in Hosea 11:4 (?). ነሠትኪ ‘you tore down’, ደምሰስኪ ‘you destroyed’, አንጻሕኪ ‘you cleansed’ (causative), አሰሰልኪ ‘you removed’ are all 2fs perfect (-ኪ). Source slip: ወደምሰስኪ አ ፡ ምሳሊሆሙ prints አ and ምሳሊሆሙ as two words; it is አምሳሊሆሙ ‘their likenesses’ (images), kept as printed. ዘጸልአ is ዘ- + ጸልአ ‘hate’; እምላዕሌሆሙ ‘from upon them’. ወለስምኪኒ is ወ- + ለ- + ስም ‘name’ + -ኪ + -ኒ ‘and for your name also’, and አስተዳለዎ ‘he prepared it’ with ዎ for ‘it’. The explanation of the name: ማክዳ is glossed ‘not so’ (አኮ ከመዝ), and the phrase ትርጒምናሁ (‘its interpretation’, ትርጒም + a suffix of ‘it’, ?) leads into the series that follows, in which she says ‘not so’ to each of her people's practices.

sentences.t: ነጸርኪ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ሕዝብኪ ፡ ዘኢይሠምር ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወትቤሊ ፡ አኮ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ አላ ፡ ይረትዕ ፡ ንስግድ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: You-looked among people-your what not-pleases God, and-you-say: not thus good but right we-worship to-God;
sentences.i: You looked at what God does not approve among your people, and you said, ‘This is not good; rather it is right that we worship God.’
sentences.n: ነጸርኪ is 2fs perfect of ነጸረ ‘look’. ዘኢይሠምር is ዘ- + ኢ- + 3ms imperfect of ሠምረ ‘be pleased with’. ትቤሊ is the 2fs of the defective ይቤ ‘say’ (the -ሊ is its ending; the glossary notes this), and the unit opens a series of six refusals the queen made: አኮ ከመዝ ሠናይ ‘it is not thus good’, አላ ‘but’, ይረትዕ ‘it is right’ (3ms, impersonal), ንስግድ ‘let us worship’ (1cp subjunctive). The pattern repeats through the next five units; I note it once.

sentences.t: አኮ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ሰጊድ ፡ ለፀሐይ ፡ አላ ፡ ሰጊድ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይረትዕ ፡ ትቤሊ ፤
sentences.l: Not thus good bowing to-sun but bowing to-God right you-say;
sentences.i: ‘It is not good to bow down to the sun, but it is right to bow down to God,’ you said.
sentences.n: ሰጊድ is the verbal noun ‘bowing, worship’; ለፀሐይ ‘to the sun’. Sun-worship is the first of the practices rejected (compare Deuteronomy 4:19, 17:3). The saying is carried by ትቤሊ at the end, ‘you say/said’.

sentences.t: አኮ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ሐቲተ ፡ ማሪት ፡ አላ ፡ ተወክሎ ፡ በእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይኄይስ ፡ ትቤሊ ፤
sentences.l: Not thus good consulting marit(?) but trust in-God better you-say;
sentences.i: ‘It is not good to consult the mārit (?), but it is better to trust in God,’ you said.
sentences.n: ሐቲተ is the accusative of the verbal noun of ሐተተ ‘question, inquire’ and takes ማሪት as object; I cannot place ማሪት, apparently a thing consulted, such as an oracle or a diviner (?). ተወክሎ is the verbal noun of ተወከለ ‘trust’ (in God, በእግዚኣብሔር); ይኄይስ ‘it is better’ (3ms of ኄሰ) replaces ይረትዕ for variety.

sentences.t: አኮ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ አስተቃስሞ ፡ ሰገል ፡ አላ ፡ አስምኮ ፡ በቅዱሰ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ይኄይስ ፡ ትቤሊ ፤
sentences.l: Not thus good consulting-omens soothsayers but trusting in-Holy-One-of Israel better you-say;
sentences.i: ‘It is not good to consult soothsayers for omens, but it is better to put one's trust in the Holy One of Israel,’ you said.
sentences.n: አስተቃስሞ is a verbal noun of a causative-tä stem (‘to ask for omens, divine’, ?) and ሰገል ‘soothsayer, diviner’ (?). አስምኮ is a verbal noun, ‘relying, taking refuge’, from አስምከ (?). ቅዱሰ እስራኤል ‘Holy One of Israel’ (construct) is the title of Isaiah (Isaiah 1:4, 5:19 and elsewhere) and of Psalm 71:22.

sentences.t: አኮ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ሠዊዕ ፡ ለአእባን ፡ ወለአዕዋም ፡ አላ ፡ ሠዊዕ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይረትዕ ፡ ትቤሊ ፤
sentences.l: Not thus good sacrificing to-stones and-to-trees but sacrificing to-God right you-say;
sentences.i: ‘It is not good to sacrifice to stones and trees, but it is right to sacrifice to God,’ you said.
sentences.n: ሠዊዕ is the verbal noun ‘sacrificing’; ለአእባን ‘to stones’ (plural of እብን); ለአዕዋም ‘to trees’, a plural I cannot confirm (taken from the sense, as in the glossary, ?). Compare Jeremiah 2:27 (‘they say to a tree, You are my father, and to a stone, You gave me birth’) and Deuteronomy 4:28.

sentences.t: አኮ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ተጠይሮ ፡ በአዕዋፍ ፡ አላ ፡ ተአምኖ ፡ በፈጣሪ ፡ ይረትዕ ፡ ትቤሊ ።
sentences.l: Not thus good augury(?) by-birds but believing in-Creator right you-say.
sentences.i: ‘It is not good to take omens from birds, but it is right to believe in the Creator,’ you said.
sentences.n: ተጠይሮ is a verbal noun which I read as ‘augury, reading omens’ (?), since the next words are በአዕዋፍ ‘by birds’; ተአምኖ is the verbal noun of ተአምነ ‘believe’; ፈጣሪ is ‘Creator’, the agent noun of ፈጠረ ‘create’. The end of the list stops at the full stop ። because a new thought begins.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ኀረይኪያ ፡ ለጥበብ ፡ ወኮነተኪ ፡ እመ ፤
sentences.l: And-then you-chose-her wisdom and-she-became-to-you mother;
sentences.i: Then you chose Wisdom, and she became a mother to you;
sentences.n: Here begins the praise of Wisdom (ጥበብ, grammatically feminine), a series of short balanced clauses of the form ‘you did X for her, and she did Y for you’, each with a feminine ‘she’ in the second verb (-ት) and a ‘you’ suffix (-ኪ). ኀረይኪያ is ኀረየ ‘choose’, 2fs perfect + -ያ ‘her’, and ለጥበብ repeats the object. ኮነተኪ is ኮነት ‘she became’ + -ኪ ‘to you’. The image recalls Sirach 15:2 (Wisdom ‘will meet him like a mother’) and Proverbs 4:6-9, 7:4 (love her, call her your sister).

sentences.t: ኀሠሥኪያ ፡ ወኮነተኪ ፡ መዝገበ ፤
sentences.l: You-sought-her and-she-became-to-you treasure;
sentences.i: You sought her, and she became a treasure to you;
sentences.n: ኀሠሥኪያ is ኀሠሠ ‘seek’, 2fs perfect + ‘her’. Compare Proverbs 2:4 (searching for wisdom as for hidden treasure) and Proverbs 8:21.

sentences.t: ተጸወንኪያ ፡ ወኮነተኪ ፡ ጥቅመ ፤
sentences.l: You-took-up-her(?) and-she-became-to-you profit;
sentences.i: You took her up (?), and she became a gain to you;
sentences.n: ተጸወንኪያ is the tä-stem of ጸወነ, whose sense is ‘carry, bear’, so ‘took her on, bore her’ (?). ጥቅመ ‘advantage, profit’ is in the accusative as predicate of ኮነት.

sentences.t: ጸህቂያ ፡ ወአፍቀረተኪ ፡ እምኵሉ ፤
sentences.l: You-delighted-in-her(?) and-she-loved-you more-than-all;
sentences.i: You delighted in her (?), and she loved you above all;
sentences.n: ጸህቂያ is the 2fs perfect of ጸሐቀ with ‘her’; the verb means ‘laugh, rejoice, play’, and I read ‘delight in’ (?), as in Proverbs 8:30-31, where Wisdom plays before God and delights in men. አፍቀረተኪ ‘she loved you’; እምኵሉ ‘more than all’ (እም ‘than’). Compare Proverbs 8:17 (‘I love those who love me’).

sentences.t: ተወከልኪያ ፡ ወሐቀፈተኪ ፡ ከመ ፡ ሕፃና ፤
sentences.l: You-trusted-her and-she-embraced-you like child;
sentences.i: You trusted in her, and she embraced you like a child;
sentences.n: ተወከልኪያ is ተወከለ ‘trust’ with the object suffix; ሐቀፈተኪ is 3fs perfect ‘she embraced’ + ‘you’. ሕፃና is ‘child’ in the accusative after ከመ, ‘like a child’. Compare Proverbs 4:8 (‘embrace her, and she will honour you’).

sentences.t: አፍቀርኪያ ፡ ወኮነተኪ ፡ በከ ፡ መ ፡ ፈቀድኪ ፤
sentences.l: You-loved-her and-she-became-to-you in-as you-wished;
sentences.i: You loved her, and she became to you as you wished;
sentences.n: Source slip: በከ ፡ መ is printed as two words; it is በከመ ‘according as, just as’, kept as printed. ፈቀድኪ is 2fs perfect of ፈቀደ ‘wish’.

sentences.t: አኀዝኪያ ፡ ወኢተኀድገኪ ፡ እስከ ፡ ዕለተ ፡ ሞትኪ ፤
sentences.l: You-held-her and-not-she-will-leave-you until day-of death-your;
sentences.i: You held fast to her, and she did not leave you until the day of your death;
sentences.n: አኀዝኪያ is አኀዘ ‘seize, hold’ + ‘her’. ኢተኀድገኪ has the 3fs prefix ተ- of the imperfect plus -ኪ ‘you’: ‘she does not forsake you’; I translate in the past to match the clauses around it. ዕለተ ሞትኪ is a double construct, ‘day of your death’.

sentences.t: አንቲ ፡ ሐዘንኪ ፡ በእንቲአሃ ፡ ወአስተፍሥሐተኪ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: You grieved for-her and-she-gladdened-you until for-ever;
sentences.i: You grieved for her sake, and she made you glad for ever;
sentences.n: አንቲ ‘you’ is the free pronoun, for emphasis. ሐዘንኪ is 2fs perfect of ሐዘነ ‘grieve’; በእንቲአሃ is በእንተ ‘for the sake of’ with the 3fs suffix in its longer stem (በእንቲአ-ሃ), referring to Wisdom. አስተፍሥሐተኪ is the causative-tä stem ‘she made you rejoice’; ‘for ever’ (እስከ ለዓለም, lit. ‘until to the age’) is the closing refrain of the whole series.

sentences.t: ጸመውኪ ፡ በእንቲአሃ ፡ ወአጥዐየተኪ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: You-fasted for-her and-she-sweetened-you until for-ever;
sentences.i: You fasted for her sake, and she made you sweet for ever;
sentences.n: ጸመውኪ is ጸመወ ‘fast’, 2fs perfect. አጥዐየተኪ is the causative of ጥዕየ ‘be sweet’, ‘she made you sweet/pleasant’ (the sense of the figure is uncertain, ?).

sentences.t: ረኀብኪ ፡ በእንቲአሃ ፡ ወአጽገበተኪ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: You-hungered for-her and-she-satisfied-you until for-ever;
sentences.i: You hungered for her sake, and she satisfied you for ever;
sentences.n: ረኀብኪ is ረኀበ ‘hunger’; አጽገበተኪ is the causative ‘she satisfied you’. Compare Matthew 5:6 and the feast of Wisdom in Proverbs 9:1-5.

sentences.t: ጸማእኪ ፡ ለጥበብ ፡ ወአርወየተኪ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: You-thirsted for-wisdom and-she-gave-you-drink until for-ever;
sentences.i: You thirsted for Wisdom, and she gave you your fill of drink for ever;
sentences.n: ጸማእኪ is ጸምአ ‘thirst’, and ለጥበብ marks what is thirsted for; አርወየተኪ is the causative of ረወየ ‘be watered’, ‘she watered you, quenched you’. Compare Isaiah 55:1 and John 4:14 (?).

sentences.t: ተመንደብኪ ፡ በእንቲአሃ ፡ ለጥበብ ፡ ወኮነተኪ ፡ ፈውሰ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: You-were-afflicted for-her for-wisdom and-she-became-to-you healing until for-ever;
sentences.i: You were afflicted for Wisdom's sake, and she became healing to you for ever;
sentences.n: ተመንደብኪ is the tä-stem of a verb from the root of ምንዱብ ‘wretched, afflicted’, so ‘you were wretched, afflicted’ (?). Here the object is stated twice, በእንቲአሃ ለጥበብ ‘on her account, on account of Wisdom’, the doubling that the series keeps. ፈውሰ ‘healing’ (accusative).

sentences.t: ጸመምኪ ፡ በእንቲአሃ ፡ ለጥበብ ፡ ወአስምዐተኪ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: You-were-deaf for-her for-wisdom and-she-made-you-hear until for-ever;
sentences.i: You were deaf for Wisdom's sake, and she made you hear for ever;
sentences.n: ጸመምኪ is ጸመመ ‘be deaf’ (?), 2fs perfect; አስምዐተኪ is the causative of ሰምዐ ‘hear’, ‘she made you hear’. The order is a series of afflictions and their remedies (hunger, thirst, sickness, deafness, blindness), as in Isaiah 35:5 (?).

sentences.t: ዖርኪ ፡ በእንቲአሃ ፡ ለጥበብ ፡ ወአብርሀተኪ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ እምነ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፡ ወዝንቱ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘኮነ ፡ እምኀበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘአፍቀርኪያ ፡ ለጥበብ ፤
sentences.l: You-were-blind for-her for-wisdom and-she-illumined-you exceedingly than sun until for-ever; and-this all which-was from-with God because you-loved wisdom;
sentences.i: You were blind for Wisdom's sake, and she lit you up for ever more than the sun; and all this came from God, because you loved Wisdom;
sentences.n: ዖርኪ is read as 2fs perfect of ዖረ ‘be blind’ (?). አብርሀተኪ is the causative ‘she made you shine’, and ፈድፋደ እምነ ፀሐይ ‘exceedingly, more than the sun’ is a comparison with እምነ ‘than’. ዘኮነ እምኀበ እግዚኣብሔር is ዘ- ‘which’ + ኮነ ‘was’ + እምኀበ ‘from (the side of)’; በእንተ ዘአፍቀርኪያ ‘because you loved her’ is በእንተ ዘ- + the perfect.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ጥበብ ፡ ወአእምሮ ፡ ወልቡና ፡ እምኀበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: For wisdom and-knowledge and-understanding from-with God it;
sentences.i: For wisdom, knowledge and understanding come from God.
sentences.n: እስመ ‘for’ gives the reason. ውእቱ ‘it is’ is a singular copula covering all three nouns, a Geʿez habit. Compare Sirach 1:1 (‘all wisdom is from the Lord’) and Proverbs 2:6.

sentences.t: ልቡና ፡ ወአእምሮ ፡ ወቀዳሜ ፡ ጥበብሰ ፡ ፈሪሀ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወአእምሮ ፡ ወመኪረ ፡ ሠናይኒ ፡ ምጽዋት ፡ ወምሕረት ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፡ እንተ ፡ ትሄሉ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ረከብኪ ፡ እግዝእትየ ፡ ኀበ ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ቅዱሰ ፡ ቅዱሳን ፡ ማእመሬ ፡ አልባብ ፡ ዘየሐትት ፡ ዘውስተ ፡ ልበ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ዘእምኀቤሁ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ኮነ ፤
sentences.l: Understanding and-knowledge and-beginning-of wisdom-indeed fear-of God and-knowledge and-counselling good-also almsgiving and-mercy until for-ever which exists(?); this all you-found my-lady with God-of Israel holy-of holies, knower-of hearts who-searches what-in heart-of man, from-with-him all was;
sentences.i: Understanding and knowledge, and as for the beginning of wisdom, the fear of God and knowledge, and also giving good counsel, almsgiving and mercy for ever, which endure (?): all this you found, my lady, with the God of Israel, the Holy of Holies, the knower of hearts, who searches what is in the heart of man, from whom everything came.
sentences.n: This is a heavy run of nouns. ቀዳሜ ጥበብሰ is the construct ቀዳሜ ‘beginning-of’ + ጥበብ + the contrastive -ሰ; the saying is the old one, ‘the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom’ (Proverbs 1:7, 9:10; Psalm 111:10; Sirach 1:14), with ፈሪሀ ‘fear-of’ in the construct. መኪረ is the accusative verbal noun ‘counselling’ and ሠናይኒ ‘good, also’; ምጽዋት ‘almsgiving’, ምሕረት ‘mercy’. እንተ ትሄሉ is the fem. relative with a 3fs imperfect of ሀሎ ‘be, exist’, ‘which exists’; what it refers to is unclear, so I read it as modifying ‘mercy’ (?). ቅዱሰ ቅዱሳን ‘Holy of Holies’ (construct, a superlative), ማእመሬ አልባብ ‘knower of hearts’ (agent noun, construct; compare Acts 1:24, 15:8 and Jeremiah 17:10), ዘየሐትት ‘who searches’ (ሐተተ ‘inquire, examine’; Psalm 7:9). ዘእምኀቤሁ ኵሉ ኮነ ‘from whom everything was’ echoes John 1:3 and Romans 11:36.

sentences.t: ወዘኒ ፡ ኮነ ፡ በፈቃደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ኮነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትምጻእ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ትኩኖ ፡ መርሐ ፡ ለንጉሥነ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ መፍቀሬ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ቀዋሚሃ ፡ ለደብተራሁ ፡ መጋቢሃ ፡ ለማኅደረ ፡ ስብሐቲሁ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-which-also was by-will-of God was: that she-come Zion into this land-of Ethiopia, and-that she-be-to-him guide for-king-our David, lover-of God, attendant-her for-tent-his, steward-her for-dwelling-of glory-his. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: And whatever has come about has come about by the will of God: that Zion should come into this land of Ethiopia and be a guide to our king David, the lover of God, the attendant of his tent, the steward of the dwelling-place of his glory.
sentences.n: ወዘኒ ኮነ is ወ- + ዘ- + -ኒ ‘and whatever (also)’; በፈቃደ is በ- + the construct ፈቃደ ‘will-of’. ትምጻእ is 3fs subjunctive (‘that she come’), with ጽዮን as the subject and ዛቲ ብሔረ ኢትዮጵያ ‘this land of Ethiopia’ (ብሔር ‘land’ in the construct). ወከመ ትኩኖ is ወ- + ከመ ‘that’ + 3fs subjunctive of ኮነ + -ኖ ‘to him’; መርሐ ‘guide’ is its predicate. ‘Our king David’ is, I take it, the Ethiopian king Menelik, who in this book receives the throne-name David (?), not the biblical David, though the title ‘lover of God’ fits the psalmist as well. መፍቀሬ ‘lover-of’ (construct) and the next two titles, ቀዋሚሃ ‘her attendant’ (‘one who stands’; -ሃ anticipates the feminine ደብተራ ‘tent’) and መጋቢሃ ‘her steward’, are appositions to David. The ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ is the usual close of a part and stays attached to this last unit.
